topic: Wireframing, Information Architecture, and User Flows
learningObjectives: Organize content using basic information architecture principles.
Create low-fidelity wireframes for application screens.
Design user flows that connect tasks and screens logically.

activities.title: Information Architecture Map
activities.instruction: Organize content into a logical application structure.

content.concept: Information architecture organizes content, features, and navigation so users can find what they need efficiently.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

activities.title: Wireframe Anatomy
activities.instruction: Explore the main regions of a wireframe.

content.concept: Wireframes define the structure, hierarchy, and placement of interface elements before detailed visual styling.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

activities.title: User Flow Sequencer
activities.instruction: Arrange screens for a common user task.

content.concept: A user flow represents the sequence of steps and screens required to complete a specific goal.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

activities.title: Wireframe Builder
activities.instruction: Compose a low-fidelity screen from interface blocks.

content.concept: Low-fidelity wireframes focus on layout and functionality without detailed colors, imagery, or visual decoration.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.
